root_cause: Every judge received the same high-level expected-output prose, but the judge prompt instructed each model call to derive its own two-to-five assertion checks.
The generated assertion IDs and decomposition therefore varied between jurors even for the same case.
The model was also asked to produce an aggregate task_success value, duplicating aggregation that should have been deterministic host logic.
correction: Each behavioral case now contains an ordered rubric with exact criterion IDs, exact binary pass descriptions, and required flags.
Every juror receives the same canonical rubric object for that case.
Jurors must return every and only the supplied criterion IDs with JSON Boolean values.
Missing, renamed, merged, split, or invented criterion IDs invalidate the grade.
The host computes task_success from the required criterion booleans; the juror no longer controls the aggregate.
Every observation records the criterion IDs and a SHA-256 rubric fingerprint.

framework_scope.implementation: custom Python evaluation harness plus Pi CLI model calls
framework_scope.conclusion: This defect was in the repository's judge prompt and schema, not in DSPx or DSPy.

validity: The suite-v2 A/A report remains useful evidence of the old evaluator's noise but cannot validate suite v3.
The criteria and judge contract changed, so the next formal step is a new suite-v3 A/A run from observation zero.
No A/B run may begin until the new A/A run passes the pre-registered thresholds.
